rubrics.criterion: After the change, the type that holds the format registry (the state that format registration writes and detection reads) does not also own any two of these unrelated domains as its own fields/methods: on-disk gathering defaults, archive-creation layout policy, extraction overwrite policy, extraction continue-on-error policy, or virtual-fs mount prefixing.
rubrics.rationale: This is the central relation of the task: one manager value gathered registry state plus five operational policy domains so that every high-level operation and its defaults lived on a single declaration. Separating the registry from the operational policies is what 'unbundle the manager' concretely means here.

rubrics.criterion: Format detection as a whole — registration, by-filename matching, by-stream matching (including detecting the archive inside a compressed layer), format listing, and choosing a format from a destination filename — is reachable through one cohesive owner whose carried state is only registry state; restricting or extending the supported formats requires changing that owner and nothing else.
rubrics.rationale: The library's detection pipeline (the loops over registered formats, the rewindable-stream matching, the compressed-layer peeling for names like .tar.gz) was lifted onto the manager. The solver must re-establish detection as a self-contained capability rather than as a side effect of sharing a receiver with unrelated domains.

rubrics.criterion: On-disk gathering — the directory walk, symlink follow/preserve handling, attribute stripping, and the disk-name-to-archive-name mapping — is owned by a single unit that holds neither registry state nor creation/extraction policies, and produces the same file list for the same explicit options as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: The walk (with its per-entry mapping and attribute machinery) was absorbed as a method so the creation convenience could apply manager-owned gathering defaults. It must return to a gathering-owned home reachable without the registry.

rubrics.criterion: The one-call archive-a-folder and extract-an-archive-to-a-directory conveniences still exist (under the same or equivalent public API), but each is now composed from explicitly cooperating owners — the detection/registry owner, the gathering unit, the extraction writer — instead of being an instance method over one type that privately holds all of the policy state.
rubrics.rationale: The prompts require the conveniences to remain available; the task's core outcome is that availability now comes from composition of the re-separated parts rather than from the omnibus receiver.

rubrics.criterion: No production (non-test) struct type in the package carries, on one declaration, instance state belonging to four or more of these areas: registry, disk-gathering defaults, creation-time layout, on-disk overwrite behavior, continue-on-error behavior, virtual-fs prefixing — regardless of the type's name or how many methods it has.
rubrics.rationale: Prevents the repair from leaving a renamed or slimmed-down all-purpose coordinator that still fuses several policy families; the maintainer complaint was about the mixing, not the type's name.

rubrics.criterion: Every package-level function exported before the maintenance change (format registration, identification, disk gathering, file-system mounting) still exists with its exact name, signature, and documented semantics, so no external caller or in-module CLI usage had to be rewritten.
rubrics.rationale: The change must be internal restructuring for the library's users; the frozen package API is the stated compatibility boundary of the task.

rubrics.criterion: The unexported helpers that format implementation files call directly — the header-sniffing read helper (readAtMost) and the stream-sizing helper (streamSizeBySeeking), plus the disk-name mapping helper used by the walk and tests — still resolve with unchanged semantics for all their existing call sites.
rubrics.rationale: A dozen format files reach these helpers across file boundaries; any re-homing of the detection/gathering machinery must keep those internal cross-file dependencies working rather than breaking the format implementations that depend on them.

rubrics.criterion: Delegation scaffolding introduced by the maintenance change was cleaned up: package-level functions that existed only as pass-through wrappers to the shared default instance are now real implementations again (or the indirection is otherwise legitimately reduced), with no wrapper surviving solely to reach a singleton.
rubrics.rationale: The maintainer observation in the prompts called out the forwarding wrappers; restoring genuine implementation bodies is the natural companion of re-homing the moved bodies.

rubrics.criterion: The ability to operate on a private/restricted set of formats — constructing a registry owner with a chosen subset or custom formats, without package-global state — either is preserved by the new structure, or was removed deliberately along with every piece of state that existed only to support it; no half-working per-instance registry state (e.g. an instance map that some operations consult and others bypass) remains.
rubrics.rationale: Restricted registries were the motivating capability of the merged design; the solver must make a coherent decision about it, not leave a split-brain registry where some paths consult instance state and others consult the package default.

rubrics.criterion: No struct fields exist whose only reason was the merged design and which no surviving method reads or writes: orphaned policy flags, unused registry maps, or leftover receiver-bound helpers with no callers are removed.
rubrics.rationale: Tests alone will not catch silently dead state left behind when the omnibus type is dismantled; dead policy fields are the residue most likely to survive a half-hearted split.

rubrics.criterion: Documentation was repaired together with the code: no doc comment still claims that package functions delegate to a default manager instance where none exists, and no type declaration still describes itself as the single high-level entry point if its responsibilities were split away.
rubrics.rationale: Stale merge-era comments actively misdirect future maintainers; both prompts ask for a package reviewers can navigate.

rubrics.criterion: The file introduced by the maintenance change (the facade for the merged type) is either deleted entirely, or retained only with declarations that belong to one coherent owner after the split, with no unused imports, dead identifiers, or method bodies left whose only ties are to the removed omnibus design.
rubrics.rationale: Continuing to route responsibility decisions through the old facade file would recreate the same centralization pressure the task exists to remove.

rubrics.criterion: A failure is present if built-in formats no longer self-register during package initialization in the same way before any use (a format dropped or duplicated, registration order changed so behavior differs, or duplicate-name registration no longer panics).
rubrics.rationale: Registry initialization behavior is the invariant most easily damaged when registration is re-homed, and it is verified by existing behavior expectations rather than by every test.

rubrics.criterion: A failure is present if, wherever extraction-to-disk writing survives, an archive entry name (absolute name, parent-directory traversal, or embedded separator tricks) can cause a write outside the destination directory.
rubrics.rationale: Path-confinement of extracted entries is a security-critical documented property of the extraction convenience; a refactor of extraction writing must not weaken it.

rubrics.criterion: A failure is present if explicitly supplied gathering options are overridden or augmented by leftover merged-design defaults (symlink following, attribute stripping), or if calling the package-level gathering function without options panics or gains behavior changes for ordinary callers.
rubrics.rationale: The merge threaded manager-owned defaults into the options path; the split must restore option precedence exactly, or explicit callers get silently different archives.

rubrics.criterion: A failure is present if the documented identification semantics changed: stream-based matching bytes/rewindability guarantees, filename-only matching when no stream is given, NoMatch routing for unrecognized input, or combined compressed-archive formats no longer resolving to a format that can both extract and create.
rubrics.rationale: Detection is the library's front door and supports documented stream-rewind contracts; re-homing detection must not disturb what callers observe for identical inputs.
